node.label: Judith R. Walkowitz
node.description: A historian of gender, sexuality and urban life who joins cultural interpretation to material and social conditions. In her Minerva interview, Walkowitz recalls Hayden White’s supervision and his introduction of Foucault as resources for her research. She also identifies E. P. Thompson’s account of lived class formation as opening a route toward gender. Her use of Foucault is selective: she questions his attention to gender and leaves more room for individual and collective agency. The prostitution study examines regulation and feminist alliances; City of Dreadful Delight asks how sexual danger and possibility were narrated across a changing city. Walkowitz cautions that reading only its scandal-centred beginning and ending misses her attempt at a simultaneous, multilayered urban history. The Soho project extends that inquiry to contested cosmopolitan spaces, rather than treating the city as either an uncomplicated refuge or a single landscape of danger.
